title: Infosys, IndiGo, Paytm and Bajaj Auto Lead India's Biggest Earnings Week of the Quarter
excerpt: More than 90 companies are set to report Q1 results this week, with Infosys reporting Thursday and IndiGo, Paytm and Eternal expected earlier in the week.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Over 90 Indian companies will report Q1 FY27 results this week, led by Infosys on July 23.
  • Infosys is projected to earn $0.21 per share with revenue around $5.1 billion.
  • Paytm and UltraTech Cement are among key companies reporting early this week.
  • IT sector faces scrutiny amid shifts in spending towards AI and mixed results from major firms.
  • Results this week could influence the Sensex and Nifty amid global market volatility.
  • More than 90 Indian companies will report Q1 FY27 results this week, headlined by Infosys on Thursday, July 23.
  • Infosys is expected to report earnings of $0.21 per share on revenue of approximately $5.1 billion, after beating estimates last quarter.
  • Monday brings UltraTech Cement and Eternal (Zomato), Tuesday brings Paytm and Dixon Technologies, and Wednesday brings Bajaj Housing Finance and Dr. Reddy's.
  • Results come amid a volatile backdrop: IT stocks are under pressure from AI-driven spending shifts, while banking and consumer stocks have shown resilience.

The Week Ahead

India's corporate earnings season hits its most consequential stretch this week, with more than 90 companies scheduled to report first-quarter results for fiscal year 2027. The lineup spans sectors from IT services and aviation to fintech and fast-moving consumer goods, giving investors a comprehensive read on the health of the Indian economy and corporate profitability.

The headliner is Infosys, which is expected to report on Thursday before US markets open. Analysts project earnings of $0.21 per share on revenue of approximately $5.1 billion. In its most recent quarter, Infosys beat the consensus estimate by $0.03, reporting $0.23 per share, and issued full-year revenue guidance of $20.5 billion to $20.9 billion.

Day-by-Day Breakdown

Monday, July 21: The week opens with UltraTech Cement, Eternal (formerly Zomato), Havells India, IDBI Bank, Oberoi Realty and PNB Housing Finance. Eternal's results will be closely watched as investors look for the food delivery giant's path to sustained profitability after its Zomato-to-Eternal rebrand.

Tuesday, July 22: One97 Communications (Paytm) reports alongside Colgate-Palmolive India, Dixon Technologies, JSW Infrastructure, Mahanagar Gas and Zee Entertainment. Paytm's numbers carry particular weight after the company navigated RBI regulatory actions last year and has been working to rebuild its payments business on firmer ground.

Wednesday, July 23: The week's most consequential day brings Infosys, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, Bajaj Housing Finance, Coforge, Persistent Systems, Tata Consumer Products and Syngene International. Infosys will set the tone for what investors can expect from the broader IT services sector in a quarter marked by cautious client spending and the ongoing rebalancing of budgets toward AI.

Later in the week: Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv, Nestle India, Shriram Finance and Kotak Mahindra Bank are among the companies expected to report toward the end of the week.

IT Sector Under Scrutiny

The IT services sector enters this results cycle under pressure. TCS, Wipro, Tech Mahindra and HCLTech have already reported, painting a mixed picture. TCS posted strong results with AI revenue hitting a $2.6 billion run rate, while Wipro saw its stock drop after brokerages slashed targets following weak guidance. HCLTech's $1.14 billion Mercedes-Benz deal provided a bright spot.

For Infosys, the key metrics will be constant-currency revenue growth, deal pipeline commentary, and any updates on how the company is positioning itself in the AI services market. The stock has dropped more than 60 percent from its 52-week high and trades at roughly $11 — a level that has attracted value-oriented investors while reflecting broader anxiety about AI's impact on traditional IT outsourcing margins.

Beyond IT: Consumer and Industrial Reads

The week also offers critical data points beyond technology. UltraTech Cement's results will signal construction and infrastructure demand. IndiGo — India's dominant airline — will reflect the health of consumer travel spending. Bajaj Finance and Kotak Mahindra Bank provide a read on credit growth and asset quality in India's financial system.

For NRI investors holding Indian equities, the week's results will likely determine the near-term direction of the Sensex and Nifty, which have been buffeted by global tech sentiment, oil price volatility tied to the Iran conflict, and foreign investor flows that recently turned positive after a $29 billion selloff.
